s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with central crusting in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek
Arborizing telangiectasias and peripheral pigment on dermoscopy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Lesions were initially observed as erythematous nodules 3 months prior
Lesions gradually increased in size
No fever, pain, or discharge from the lesions
Patient has a history of kidney transplant in 2004
Patient is immunocompromised
Lesions are firm with central ulceration and hemorrhagic crusting
Dermoscopy showed arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
Histopathological examination showed extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified on histopathological examination

per_call: Cutaneous leishmaniasis due to Leishmania braziliensis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions and intracellular yeasts on histopathological examination

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and histopathological findings, including intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with skin lesions and potential exposure to fungal pathogens

shortlist.label: Coccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and potential for fungal infection in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible fungal infection in an immunocompromised patient with skin lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos on histopathological examination is characteristic of Cryptococcosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with broad-based budding yeasts, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Histoplasmosis usually presents with smaller yeasts and a different clinical context

rejected.label: Coccidioidomycosis
rejected.why: Coccidioidomycosis is typically associated with the southwestern United States and presents with spherules, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
rejected.why: Paracoccidioidomycosis is typically associated with Latin America and presents with a distinct 'pilot's wheel' appearance, not seen in this case
